prerequisites: kinematics and statics of rigid bodies

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge of the basic tools for the description of the mechanical behavior of one-dimensional elastic structures and of elastic bodies. In particular, the student must understand and operate with the fundamental issues of deformation, stress states and constitutive equations with particular attention to the case of linearly elastic structures and solids.
Knowledge of the fundamental concepts of the strength of materials both from a theoretical and experimental point of view.

syllabus_topics: Mathematical fundamentals: Fundamentals on Tensor algebra, Tensors, Second order tensors, Components, Cartesian representation and polar decomposition, Eigenvalues and eigenvectors.

Strain: Deformation of continuum bodies, Strain measures, Linear theory, Principal stretches and principal direction of strain, Examples of elementary deformations, Representation formula of infinitesimal strain, Compatibility equations.

Stress: Force system, Axioms of Euler, Stress tensor, Equilibrium equations, Principal stresses and principal directions of stress, Mohr’s circle, Examples of elementary states of stress, General theorems: work done and virtual work.

Constitutive equations and the elastic problem: General aspects, Linear elastic and hyperelastic materials, Statement of the elastic equilibrium problem, Energy theorems, Unicity theorem of Kirchhoff, Elastic isotropy, General aspects, Representation formula, Technical moduli and restrictions on their values.
Saint-Venant’s problem: General formulation, Normal force, Bending, Torsion, Shear, Combined normal force and bending.
Strength criteria: General aspects, Maximum and minimum normal stress criterion, Maximum shear stress criterion, Maximum and minimum strain criterion, Energy criterion, Safety evaluation.

Statically determinate beams and frames – Kinematics: Preliminary concepts of kinematics of rigid bodies, Plane case, Linear kinematics of rigid bodies, Definition of beam, Plane beam, Kinematic characterization of external and internal constraints, Kinematic analysis, Theorem of kinematical chains.

Statically determinate beams and frames – Statics: Force systems for beams, Axioms of equilibrium, Definition of internal forces, Equilibrium theorems for plane beams, Static characterization of external and internal constraints, Static analysis of beams and frames, Solution of problems on statically determinate structures, Principle of virtual works.
Elastic beams: Elastica for normal force, shear, bending and torsion; thermal deformations, Virtual work equation, Evaluation of displacements and rotations.
Statically indeterminate beams and frames: Solution of statically indeterminate beams and frames, Force method and Moment method.
Design and safety evaluation of structures: Solution of simple problems on design and safety evaluation of structures.

assessment_methods.method: Two partial tests (exemption from written test)

assessment_rules: The exam consists of an oral examination preceded by a written test, covering both modules. Passing the written test (minimum 18/30) gives access to the final oral examination (minimum 18/30). Students can be exempted from the written test by passing two partial tests. A student can also take the exam only through an interview, which is divided into two parts, a problem-solving part followed by a theoretical part, with the same evaluation criteria.
